content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To write a movie, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Brainstorm core high-concept ideas (2 days)
Step 2. Research the historical setting (1 week)
Step 3. Develop the protagonist's back-story (3 days)
Step 4. Write the final climax scene (2 days)
Step 5. Draft the initial scene index cards (4 hours)
Step 6. Arrange scenes on a storyboard (1 day)
Step 7. Write the first ten pages of the script (5 days)
Step 8. Register the title with the copyright office (1 hour)
Step 9. Create a list of primary locations (2 days)
Step 10. Refine the dialogue for the main characters (4 days)
Step 11. Choose the genre and tone (6 hours)
Step 12. Format the script for industry standards (3 hours)
Step 13. Create a mood board for visual style (1 day)
Step 14. Write a one-page plot summary (2 hours)
Step 15. Complete the second draft of the script (2 weeks)
Step 16. Research legal clearances for brand names (3 days)
Step 17. Write the middle act sequences (10 days)
Step 18. Conduct a table read with actors (5 hours)
Step 19. Define the character archetypes (1 day)
Step 20. Polish the final shooting script (1 week)
Step 21. Write the supporting character descriptions (3 days)
Step 22. Map out the character arcs (4 days)
Step 23. Design a promotional poster mockup (6 hours)
Step 24. Write a detailed story beat sheet (2 days)
Step 25. Outline the subplots (2 days)
Step 26. Conduct an initial thematic analysis (12 hours)
Step 27. Draft the transition scenes (3 days)
Step 28. Write the opening hook (1 day)
Step 29. Develop the primary antagonist (4 days)
Step 30. Sketch the world-building details (2 days)
Step 31. Compose a three-act structure outline (1 day)
Step 32. Select a working title (30 minutes)
Step 33. Write the script's first draft conclusion (4 days)
Step 34. Review the script for pacing issues (2 days)
Step 35. Deepen the emotional stakes of the hero (2 days)
Step 36. Interview subject matter experts (3 days)
Step 37. Identify the central conflict (1 day)
Step 38. Get feedback from a professional reader (1 week)
Step 39. Revise the script based on peer notes (5 days)
Step 40. Prepare the final pitch deck (2 days)
